summary:
Órbita Frontera is an educational space-exploration game built around a pixel-art expedition. Players begin on the Moon, explore the environment, collect materials, build and maintain a base, and progress through mission-inspired activities. The project combines an exploratory gameplay loop with a cinematic introduction and an interactive training sequence. Its purpose is to turn space-science themes into an accessible playable experience, encouraging curiosity, preparation and problem-solving before the expedition advances toward Mars.
The game presents space exploration through actions rather than exposition alone: players move through an environment, gather resources, interact with equipment and respond to gameplay challenges. The experience connects learning themes with exploration and resource management.
details:
The implementation extends the existing game rather than replacing its core experience. The team requested a cinematic opening, interactive training in place of the previous quiz, preservation of the custom character, and continuity with the existing mechanics.

PLAYER EXPERIENCE Keeps the new sequence compatible with the existing game. Maintains continuity with the project's visual identity and asset attributions/licences. The requested changes preserve the custom character and existing mechanics while adding a more narrative opening and hands-on training. The training sequence uses its own state so that its activities do not consume or overwrite the expedition's resource state. SCOPE NOTE The eight challenges are an educational game sequence. Their order, timing, assessment logic and pass conditions are design choices created for this experience; they should not be described as mandatory astronaut tests or official NASA qualification criteria.
